Aer Lingus has now equipped its entire A321 fleet with Starlink. 

Passengers can enjoy free, ultra-fast Wi-Fi while flying across the Atlantic.

The airline expects its full long-haul fleet to be connected by the end of 2026.

Starlink is turning in-flight Wi-Fi into a completely different experience.

Tesla app adds passkey support for passwordless sign-in.

Tesla app version 4.61.0 now lets users sign in with Face ID, Touch ID, or their device passcode instead of a traditional password.
Passkeys use cryptographic credentials stored on the device, making them highly resistant to phishing and password-based credential leaks.
The feature began rolling out to iOS users on September 19, 2026, with Android fingerprint support expected soon.
Users can enable it under Security & Privacy > Sign In Management in the Tesla app.

Tesla is making account security faster, simpler, and less dependent on passwords.

NASA awards SpaceX three additional crewed missions to the International Space Station.

SpaceX will launch NASA’s Crew-15, Crew-16, and Crew-17 missions aboard Falcon 9 and Crew Dragon from Florida.
The updated CCtCap contract brings SpaceX’s total number of NASA crewed missions to 17, supporting sustained U.S. access to the ISS.
The missions will continue using Crew Dragon as NASA’s primary commercial crew spacecraft for transporting astronauts to and from the station.

SpaceX’s Crew Dragon program continues to play a central role in maintaining crewed access to the ISS.

Tesla Semi Stamping Out the Body

This throwback video from August 2025 is the result of auspicious timing and maybe a heads-up from the head of the semi program.

Schuler stamping presses made the arduous trip from Giga Texas without the benefit of using any major highways. 

In addition, countless permits were required from each jurisdiction along the way. 

Why do you think Tesla took delivery and then stored these presses at Giga Texas for over a year before shipping them to Nevada?

WHY ROBOTAXI

DRIVING IS THE DANGEROUS MODE.
THE ROBOT IS THE SAFE MODE.

Most people still think self-driving is a nice-to-have.

That's only half the story.

Elon Musk:

"You'll be able to tell your car take me home, go here, go there, anything, & it'll just do it. At an order of magnitude safer than a person."

"In fact, in the distant future, I think people may outlaw driving cars because it's too dangerous."

That's why Robotaxi matters.

• 1× human driver — today's default risk
• ~10× safer — the bar he named
• Unsupervised miles — the product path
• Manual driving — the mode that may get outlawed

Safer isn't a feature.
It's the default.

BREAKING: Canada is getting its first Tesla Megawatt Charging System sites. 🇨🇦⚡️

R.R. Plett Trucking will begin installing Tesla’s 1.2 MW chargers in Langley and Kamloops next month.

• 12 Tesla Semi trucks on order
• Deliveries expected June 2027
• Charging time could drop from ~3 hours to ~30 minutes
• Plans underway to electrify the Vancouver–Calgary trucking corridor

The MCS network is being built to enable double-shift operations and support longer-haul electric trucking. 🚛🔋

Source: Electric Autonomy

STARSHIP IS THE CATALYST FOR ORBITAL COMPUTE

“With Starship on the AI side, it is a configuration largely the same satellites from the bus side. But then you're changing the payload and putting more solar on there and putting radiators… giving us the capability to put a whole constellation of satellites up for the orbital compute. And so all of that is driven by Starship.”

— Bret Johnsen, SpaceX CFO
(BlackRock Tony Kim fireside · SpaceX Mission Control)

Video

NOT DATA CENTERS IN SPACE — RACKS IN SPACE

“It's probably better to say racks in space simply because it's a whole constellation of satellites… largely the same satellite bus… putting more solar, putting a radiator on it, and putting compute chips instead of communications chips. We've already flown 11,000 satellites in space, so it's not hard to understand why we're going to fly thousands more… we have the hardest pieces — launch and connectivity — already done.”

— Bret Johnsen, SpaceX CFO
(BlackRock Tony Kim fireside · SpaceX Mission Control)

Video

HOLY GRAIL OF ROCKETRY — FULLY REUSABLE STARSHIP

“That's this revolutionary, intended to be very quickly here hopefully in a matter of months, fully reusable rocket — the holy grail of rocketry that's gonna drive another 10x improvement in cost per kilogram to orbit and really open up the entire industry for us.”

— Bret Johnsen, SpaceX CFO
(BlackRock Tony Kim fireside · SpaceX Mission Control)

Video

V3 STARLINK: 10× V2 · 1 TBPS · 20× FALCON 9 PER LAUNCH

“One launch of Starship with these V3 satellites will be the equivalent of 20 times what we were flying with Falcon 9. So each satellite is about a 10x, and then you get even more capability. Each satellite is a terabit. And so when you're flying 50 or 60 satellites per flight… 50 terabits of bandwidth per launch.”

— Bret Johnsen, SpaceX CFO
(BlackRock Tony Kim fireside · SpaceX Mission Control)
